If all details vanish, an even coordinate is zero and an odd coordinate is a section applied to the next-level coordinate with smaller index. Strong induction at all starting scales gives zero; no scalar substitute or norm-convergence claim is used.

The guaranteed prefix is k+1<2^N, so its first excluded coordinate is k=2^N-1. In the identity-bonding scalar hierarchy, the constant residual one has restored remainder 2^N at that coordinate. The corrected next-coordinate wording is sharp, including N=0.

Resolution.Obj is an arbitrary natural-number-indexed type family; FinitelyObserved factors each output coordinate through some input level and has no Finite instance. The added explanation matches these definitions and keeps the later finite-fiber existence hypothesis separate.

Monotonicity gives a=phi(n)<=b=phi(n+1). Each term rhoY[a,k] r_k rhoX[k+1,b] maps X_b to Y_a, exactly the sampled residual fiber. At repeated levels the sum is empty and equals zero. Substitution of the fine differential telescopes to the sampled differential. Boundedness still requires the later uniform gap bound.

The cocycle/gauge formulas use group multiplication in fixed order and only assume groups and restriction homomorphisms. Need not be abelian states the intended lack of commutativity without treating separate groups as elements that commute.

The unique nonidentity C2 arrow requires p*p=1, which includes p=1. CocycleExamples.loopCocycleEquiv has precisely the subtype {p // p*p=1}. In S3 these are identity plus three transpositions, with two conjugacy classes. The remaining phrase nonidentity involution has the conventional order-two meaning.

The view category has two objects but the coefficient group H is arbitrary. The marked-arrow equations solve uniquely as a0=psi^-1 phi and a1=(rprime)^-1 a0 r in that order; no finiteness of H is needed. Two-view is the accurate scope.

hunk_matrix.evidence: Every a has finite norm, so ran(T) is the increasing union over M>=0 of T(closedBall(0,M)), whether or not the full range is closed. In the Hilbert setting each budget image is closed by a weak subsequence of bounded lifts and convex by linearity. The revision removes the accidental suggestion that nonclosedness was assumed.

The support pairing is <a,T*z>. If T*z=0 it vanishes for every feasible a; if M=0 the only feasible a is zero. Hence every feasible pairing, not merely its maximum, is zero in either exceptional case. For M>0 and T*z nonzero, a=M*T*z/||T*z|| attains M*||T*z||.

The new assumption matches S:H ->L[real] Y in BudgetRobustness.lean. Both profiles use the same H norm and same ball. For each feasible a, residual-norm difference is at most delta+eta*M; taking infima in both directions proves WR05. The nominal dual lower bound follows by subtracting this allowance from WR04. No changing-kernel comparison is claimed.

When b=P_closure(ranT)r is attained, the preimages of b are exactly the least-squares corrections by orthogonal decomposition. The minimum-norm preimage a-dagger is the same selected limit as in WR08. Reordering the phrase does not change the selected object.

r and rtilde are vectors in the same real Hilbert target, with the same T and positive alpha. Adding vectors merely makes their type explicit; the data-sensitivity quantifiers and constants remain unchanged.

For alpha>0, T=0 gives g=alpha*e and equality in ||e||<=||g||/alpha. T=sqrt(alpha)I gives g=2alpha*e and equality in ||Te||<=||g||/(2sqrt(alpha)). The names now identify the correct first two estimates without claiming simultaneous sharpness for all operators.

For R:S->K, faithfulness is injectivity of each map Hom_S(A,B)->Hom_K(RA,RB); fullness is its surjectivity for every A,B; essential surjectivity is that every K-object is isomorphic to some RA. The revised paragraph gives these exact quantifiers and distinguishes equality from isomorphism.

For inverse isometric transports, the reversed residual equals minus the inverse transport applied to the forward residual, so their norms agree. Duplication doubles the sum of squared residual norms and multiplies its square root by sqrt(2), leaving the exact kernel and source distance unchanged. The least gain 1 becomes 1/sqrt(2); the maximum residual norm is unchanged.

With H_n=sum_{j=1}^n 1/j (H_0=0), the harmonic increment is 1/(n+1). The other residual-coordinate increment is 1/((n+1)(n+2)); the maximum norm therefore gives the claimed steps. Dividing by residual 1/(n+1) yields C_n=1 for drift and C_n=1/(n+2) for the convergent path.

On ker p=span(2,1), a=(2c,c) has squared norm 5c^2. Thus J(c)=(1-2c)^2+5c^2=9(c-2/9)^2+5/9. The stated optimizer and objective follow. Omitting the Gram factor gives c=2/5, whose actual objective is 1/25+20/25=21/25. The Euclidean declaration is necessary and correct.
